s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive proximal muscle weakness with inflammatory and autoimmune features
salient_findings: Progressive proximal muscle weakness over 2 months
Morning stiffness of small hand joints
key_facts: 14-year-old girl presented with progressive proximal muscle weakness
Difficulty combing hair and rising from a chair
Morning stiffness of both small hand joints lasting about 30 minutes
Poor appetite without fever or weight loss
Symmetric muscle strength of 4/5 in upper limbs and 3/5 in lower limbs
Brisk reflexes more pronounced on the left
Tenderness at proximal interphalangeal and metacarpophalangeal joints
Elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Suppressed TSH and elevated free T4

shortlist.label: Juvenile Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive proximal muscle weakness, elevated inflammatory markers, and skin findings are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Overlap of muscle weakness, inflammatory markers, and autoimmune features such as elevated anti-thyroglobulin antibodies and antinuclear antibody titer

shortlist.label: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Morning stiffness, joint tenderness, and elevated inflammatory markers are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Hashimoto's Thyroiditis
shortlist.why_kept: Markedly elevated anti-thyroglobulin antibodies and history of thyroiditis are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Necrotizing Autoimmune Myopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive proximal muscle weakness and elevated inflammatory markers, although normal creatine kinase levels are less typical for this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of progressive proximal muscle weakness, morning stiffness, and tenderness at proximal interphalangeal and metacarpophalangeal joints, along with elevated inflammatory markers and normal creatine kinase, are consistent with Juvenile Dermatomyositis. The presence of leukopenia, microcytic anemia, and elevated anti-thyroglobulin antibodies also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
rejected.why: While the patient has some features of Mixed Connective Tissue Disease, such as elevated anti-thyroglobulin antibodies and leukopenia, the primary presentation of progressive proximal muscle weakness and specific muscle strength findings are more characteristic of Juvenile Dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms of morning stiffness and joint tenderness could suggest Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis, but the primary complaint of progressive proximal muscle weakness and the presence of bilateral sacroiliitis on MRI are not typical of this condition.

rejected.label: Hashimoto's Thyroiditis
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of thyroiditis and elevated anti-thyroglobulin antibodies, the primary presentation of progressive proximal muscle weakness and specific muscle strength findings are not characteristic of Hashimoto's Thyroiditis.

rejected.label: Necrotizing Autoimmune Myopathy
rejected.why: The patient's normal creatine kinase level and lack of significant muscle necrosis on laboratory studies make Necrotizing Autoimmune Myopathy less likely.
